3090138.findings: Four photos: full framed view, figure close-up, inscription close-up and a seal close-up (all enlarged and checked). Brush painting in ink and colour on paper (yellowed ground, painted gold-yellow sky and clouds, green sea): a woman in Tang-style dress with flowers in her hair playing a long flute, standing on a pink lotus petal over waves with a lotus leaf behind her. The inscription reads 荷花仙子 (Lotus Fairy), which fits the lotus immortal He Xiangu named in the title. The cursive signature beneath appears to read 壬午 (a cyclical year) then 孫菁 (artist name), but my reading is uncertain. Red seals: a round one above the title, two small square ones under the signature, a tall rectangular one at upper right and a small one at lower right; none could be deciphered. Two web searches (19/10/2026) for the name as read found no matching artist. Style is a bright modern studio gongbi look (soft ink-wash hair, fine-line face), not an early or museum-style work. Framed behind glass in a thick black frame with a dark backing board; no dealer label or older inscription seen.
3090138.condition: Glazed, so the paper surface cannot be judged; paper looks clean with even toning and no tears or foxing visible through the glass; strong glare reflections. Frame is plain black timber with scuffs and a small lighter scuff on the top edge.
3090138.reason: Bright modern decorative gongbi painting with an unidentified cursive signature and unreadable seals; no sign of a known artist, modest value.
3090138.marks_read: Inscription 荷花仙子 (Lotus Fairy); signature appears 壬午 孫菁 (uncertain, artist not traced); five red seals, none deciphered.

3090139.findings: Six photos (front, lock plate close-up, two close-ups of a paper label, back/side with paper strip, drawers open). Narrow four-drawer Japanese chest (tansu); the title's 'tansy' is a misspelling that will make it harder to find in searches. Plain timber, probably sugi (Japanese cedar) with a dark worn finish. Each drawer has an iron lock plate with keyhole and boss and a forged iron swing handle; an iron carrying ring is on the side; drawer interiors are pale unfinished softwood. Remnants of old paper labels with ink characters survive on some drawer fronts (heavily abraded; one character looks like 甲 or 田, the rest unreadable). A pasted paper strip down the back carries two columns of cursive Japanese brush writing (kuzushiji), not legible at this resolution; old paper like this is commonly seen on genuine old merchant chests and supports age. No maker's name, seal or date found. Construction and fittings look Meiji to Taisho in style, which fits the 'early 1900's' title.
3090139.condition: Heavy honest wear: scraped and flaking surface, scuffs and dark staining, chipped and worn edges on the drawer rails and top, paper label remnants. Iron fittings are rusty but complete; drawers slide out and look complete; keys not seen; no obvious structural cracks in the photos.
3090139.reason: Genuine looking early 1900s Japanese four-drawer tansu with original iron fittings and old writing, misspelt in the title so likely to be missed by searchers; solid mid-range piece.
3090139.marks_read: No maker marks. Abraded ink characters on paper labels on drawer fronts (partly 甲 or 田, rest illegible); cursive Japanese writing on pasted paper strip at the back, illegible.

3090140.findings: Five photos (front, side with fixing hole, rough back face, two further angles), all enlarged. A carved piece of pale, fine-grained, pitted stone (looks more like limestone than sandstone as titled) in the form of a Gothic-style corbel or bracket: a rounded bowl carved with deep undercut leaf forms and drilled round 'eyes' between the leaves, tapering to a moulded stem with stacked rings and a small point (photos 1 and 2 show it stem-up). The back is a flat rough broken or sawn face with orange iron staining, so it was taken from a wall, and a round fixing or dowel hole shows in the side face. Drilled-eye foliage like this is typical of late medieval French carving but is also copied in 19th century Gothic revival work and in modern reproductions, so age cannot be confirmed from photos. Tiny pink or red trace and white deposits inside a couple of carved recesses (old paint, plaster or lime, not identified). No mason's mark, inscription or date seen, only the auction tag. The title does not say it is a corbel with foliate carving.
3090140.condition: Heavy weathering and pitting, some losses to leaf edges and the top rings, broken back face with rust marks; a hairline seam or crack runs down the centre of the front. Stone looks sound overall with no major break, but weight and any hidden cracks cannot be judged.
3090140.reason: Carved stone Gothic-style foliate corbel from France (per title) that could be a genuine old architectural fragment worth well above a garden ornament; age unproven and it may be a later copy.
3090140.marks_read: none (auction tag only; no mason's marks or inscriptions)

3090141.condition: Marks and light staining on the cream side, a loose length of cord or piping at one edge, general dust; frames and hinges look sound and the panels fold flat.

3090144.findings: Two photos, both sides (also checked with boosted contrast for scratched writing). 3090146.findings: Four photos: the group of six, a close view of two chairs, the carved roundel and a seat. Set of six matching Edwardian style dining chairs: high backs with a shaped top rail, a carved roundel with a stylised Art Nouveau scroll on a punched (stippled) ground, three slender slats below, drop-in seats in later pale green damask, cabriole front legs, plain rear legs and side and back stretchers. The set looks complete and matched. The timber is honey-brown with a fine close grain; I could not see the ray fleck expected of oak, so 'English oak' cannot be confirmed from the photos (could be oak or another hardwood such as ash or an Australian timber). No maker's label, stamp or number seen; seat undersides and rails are not photographed.
3090146.condition: Good, clean looking polish with light wear; seat fabric is tidy with a few small spots; no broken legs, splats or repairs visible in the photos; stability and seat frame joints not shown.
3090146.reason: Complete matched set of six Edwardian carved-back dining chairs in good order; sets are worth more than singles and the timber and origin may be better than the title suggests.

3090147.findings: Single photo. Rectangular tray with raised rims on the long sides and a chip-carved geometric design: a large central rosette in a lozenge with two smaller side rosettes, four corner rosettes and zig-zag borders, in stained fruitwood or walnut-type timber. Two end handles with turned wooden grips on brass wire mounts look like later additions (a paper tag is on the left handle). No maker's mark, date or signature on the face; underside not shown. Chip carving of this kind is common folk art (Frisian and Dutch, but also Scandinavian and Swiss), so the Dutch claim is plausible but unproven, and the age looks early to mid 20th century.
3090147.condition: Light wear on the carving, small knocks and slight gaps at the rim corners; handles intact; no splits seen on the face.
3090147.reason: Common chip-carved folk tray with later looking handles, unmarked, modest value.

3090148.findings: Two photos. Low rectangular trestle coffee table with a plank top and moulded edge, two shaped trestle ends (pierced waist) each with a cross-shaped key peg through the tenon, a plinth foot at each end and a rail or stretcher underneath. The pegged joints and chunky shapes fit the 'peg and dowel Arts and Crafts' description, but similar pieces were made well into the 1930s to 1950s, so age cannot be pinned down. The top looks light and plain, and the grain is not clearly oak in the photos. No maker's label, stamp or brand seen; the underside and stretcher are not photographed. Small white stock stickers on the top (not maker's marks).
3090148.condition: Light surface wear: faint scratches and small marks on the top with a slightly bleached centre and mild edge wear; joints look tight and no obvious damage.
3090148.reason: Solid pegged oak trestle coffee table in a sought-after Arts and Crafts style; attribution and age unproven and unmarked, so a modest candidate.

3090149.findings: Two photos: the whole folded rug and a close-up of the labels (enlarged and rotated to read). The woven label reads 'THE GEELONG R S & S [WOOLLEN] MILLS' around a Rising Sun badge with 'PURE WOOL' and a sheep, with wattle sprigs, and 'RETSOL RUGS' beneath, so this is a Retsol rug (Returned Soldiers' and Sailors' co-operative mill, Geelong), a brand the title does not name. A second black woven tag in red script reads 'Lindsay' (the tartan name); the check is red and green. A web search (19/10/2026) found museum records, for example https://www.awm.gov.au/collection/C978938, describing this label type and saying the mill's labels from 1920 to the late 1930s carried the Rising Sun and wattle; this rug may be of that era or later, which I cannot tell from the photos. Fringed at both ends.
3090149.condition: Bright, clean colours and full fringes; a little fluff and a few stray white threads in the fringe; no holes, stains or moth damage seen on the visible folded areas, but the rest of the rug is not shown.
3090149.reason: Retsol rug (Geelong returned servicemen's co-operative mill) with a Lindsay tartan tag, brand not named in the title; documented Australian textile history, a modest collectable in clean condition.
3090149.marks_read: Woven label: THE GEELONG R S & S [WOOLLEN] MILLS, PURE WOOL with Rising Sun and sheep, RETSOL RUGS; separate tag: Lindsay.

3090151.findings: Three photos: the lot, the hat on a stand and the label inside the crown. A dark charcoal to black low-crowned fur-felt hat (short topper or riding hat shape) with a ribbed silk band, a side bow loop, a bound brim and a cream satin lining. The paper label in the crown reads 'LINCOLN BENNETT & Co. HATTERS PICCADILLY LONDON' in gold on a blue shield beside a red and gold royal arms, so the hat is by a well known London court hatter (the title says only 'English made'). No size mark or date visible. Gloves in a wicker basket: a pair of tan suede or pigskin gloves, two string-back (crochet back) gloves with brown leather trim, a yellow suede pair in a clear packet with press studs, and a clear bag holding more brown and tan leather gloves; no glove brand legible. A web search (19/10/2026) describes Lincoln Bennett as a Piccadilly hatter with royal patronage (https://www.campaignfurniture.com/artists/lincoln-bennett).
3090151.condition: Hat looks clean and well kept with an even nap, a few lighter fibres and light dust, no crushing or brim damage seen; lining and label slightly toned with small spotting at the lower edge of the label; band intact. The loose gloves show wear, some pairs are still bagged.
3090151.reason: Fur-felt hat with a clear Lincoln Bennett & Co Piccadilly label and royal arms (maker not named in the title), in good order, plus riding gloves.
3090151.marks_read: Crown label: LINCOLN BENNETT & Co. HATTERS PICCADILLY LONDON with royal arms. No marks on gloves.
